about: Which upstream Franken libraries this workspace reuses, adapts or only references, at which exact revisions, and the machine-checked reason. Each row names the test that holds it (tests/p06/test_ledger.py) and the condition under which the row should be deleted. A row is not a report: when its pin does not resolve, its ancestry claim is false, or its recorded upstream bytes change, a test fails.
sibling_root_default: the parent directory of this repository

pins.role: the workspace's one Asupersync pin: E06's inventory (toolchain/results/e06/upstream/) and P05's source scan (tests/p05/upstream_scan.json) were both taken at it
the revision FIRMWARE_ASSESSMENT.md (2026-11-04) read; an ancestor of the pin above, so it is superseded by it, not a second pin

upstreams.reason: The legacy-runtime route (64-bit atomics and the runtime-core gates) is P05's (docs/contracts/p05.md). P06 adds no Asupersync dependency.
upstreams.gate: P06-PIN-001 (both revisions resolve, the older is an ancestor of the newer), P06-ISO-001 (no workspace manifest or lock entry names asupersync)
upstreams.delete_when: P05's production adapter consumes Asupersync at the pin; the row then moves to P05's contract

pins.role: franken_kernel/ is a directory of the Asupersync repository, so it is pinned by the same revision

upstreams.reason: At the pin the crate is the suite's identifier substrate (TraceId, DecisionId, PolicyId, SchemaVersion), not a task or budget type, and the renderer's own run, case and correlation identifiers are already defined and tested in franken-control. Its manifest also leaves serde's default `std` feature on (`serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }`), so it is not effectively `no_std` until upstream changes that.
upstreams.gate: P06-PIN-002 (the recorded manifest line is at the pin; if upstream changes it the row must be re-judged)
upstreams.delete_when: a workspace crate needs one of its identifiers and the serde line is fixed upstream, or the owner decides not to reuse it

pins.role: the revision FIRMWARE_ASSESSMENT.md read; an ancestor of the pin above

upstreams.disposition: semantic reference, rejected as a source of ABI numbers
upstreams.consumed_by: nothing; tests/p06 reads its errno table at the pin as the oracle that a generic table is wrong on MIPS
upstreams.reason: Its errno module is the generic (x86_64/PowerPC) numbering with a thread-local cell. Of the ten network errnos in franken-platform's net module it defines nine (EMSGSIZE is absent), all nine equal PowerPC's number and all nine differ from MIPS's. Dropping its x86_64/aarch64 compile_error gates would therefore build and misread MIPS on every one of them. The numbers in franken-platform come from the libc crate's per-architecture files, the E03 probe and the E03 guest transcripts instead.
upstreams.gate: P06-ORACLE-001 (every upstream network errno equals PowerPC's number and differs from MIPS's)
upstreams.delete_when: FrankenLibC carries per-architecture errno tables for the two big-endian ABIs, at which point this oracle becomes a witness and the row becomes 'adapted'

upstreams.reason: U01's journal (crates/franken-journal) was written from scratch; docs/contracts/u01.md says no upstream frankenfs code is adopted. No raw-flash or filesystem support is claimed anywhere.
upstreams.gate: P06-PIN-001 (the revision resolves), P06-ISO-001 (no manifest or lock entry names an ffs crate)
upstreams.delete_when: a storage algorithm is adopted from it, with its own tests and revision in that contract

upstreams.reason: Control leases, epochs and fencing are implemented natively in franken-session (G01) and franken-control (N02). LocalAPI delegation is not native Tailscale and nothing here claims it.
upstreams.gate: P06-PIN-001 (the revision resolves), P06-ISO-001 (no manifest or lock entry names an fr-* crate)
upstreams.delete_when: a lease or media-queue algorithm is adopted from it, with its own tests and revision in that contract

crates_that_must_not_be_direct_dependenc._why: libc is an FFI table the lock carries for other reasons; the platform layer and its leaf issue raw calls themselves (the one counted unsafe edge) and must not grow a dependency that would make a build look portable by importing someone else's constants.
